classification.difficultyReason: Derive the geometric area ratio from recursively inscribed figures, then sum infinitely many disjoint shaded regions.

inlines.text: A circle is inscribed in a square of side length 2, with the area between the square and the circle shaded.
We then recursively inscribe a scaled down copy of the same figure in the inner-most circle. The first two iterations are shown below.
If the procedure is repeated infinitely many times, then what is the total shaded area?

spec.description: Axis-aligned square with a concentric inscribed circle; only square-minus-circle regions are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Square side 2; circle radius 1; circle tangent to all four square sides.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure contains no answer.

spec.description: Two concentric, axis-aligned square/circle pairs; inner-square corners touch the outer circle.
spec.mathematics: Outer square half-side 1; inner square half-side 1/sqrt(2); each circle radius equals its square half-side.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied recursive construction only; no numerical answers or added labels.

spec.description: Three concentric, axis-aligned square/circle pairs; intervening circle-minus-square regions remain white.
spec.mathematics: Square half-sides 1, 1/sqrt(2), 1/2; each new square has its four corners on the preceding circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied recursive construction only; no numerical answers or added labels.

answer.short:
$8-2\pi$ square units.

Each successive shaded area is half the previous one; sum the GP with first term $4-\pi$.
answer.worked:
The first circle has radius $1$, so the first shaded area is $4-\pi$.

Let $x$ be the side length of the next square. Its diagonal is the diameter of the first circle.
$$\begin{align*}
x^2+x^2&=2^2\\
2x^2&=4\\
x^2&=2\\
x&=\sqrt{2}
\end{align*}$$
The linear scale factor between successive square/circle pairs is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. Therefore, their shaded areas have common ratio
$$r=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2=\frac12.$$
The shaded regions are disjoint. Since $|r|<1$, their total area is
$$\begin{align*}
A&=(4-\pi)\left(1+\frac12+\left(\frac12\right)^2+\cdots\right)\\
A&=\frac{4-\pi}{1-\frac12}\\
A&=2(4-\pi)\\
A&=8-2\pi\text{ square units}.
\end{align*}$$
